title: An omitted argument reuses the current carrier value
summary: Use the observed OT/OL argument frames to test a bounded ellipsis rule: after a visible Y, AIIN, AIN or OR sets the current argument carrier, a following card without a new argument should reuse that value rather than silently selecting a new one.

design.mechanism: Argument values persist across an immediately following card only when no replacement argument is visibly written; OT/OL determines opening versus continuation, while the carrier value remains the same.
design.unit: complete OT/OL state cards with a final visible argument and an immediate successor classified as argument-bearing or argument-free
design.contrast: argument-free successor with inherited carrier versus successor with a visible replacement argument; compare against a null model allowing silent carrier changes
design.prediction: Argument-free successors preserve the preceding carrier value; visible Y/AIIN/AIN/OR successors replace it. The distinction should hold across the six observed OT/OL/DY envelopes.
design.falsifier: Any predeclared set of argument-free successors that systematically changes carrier value, or inherits an incompatible/empty value despite a fixed preceding carrier, falsifies the ellipsis rule.
design.scope: GDT559 observed state-card stream; independent semantic binding availability_unknown because the carrier labels remain working hypotheses, not externally authored meanings
design.related: Distinct from prior antecedent/reference and role-position proposals: this tests omission-based value inheritance inside an exact argument slot, not lexical anaphora, line breaks, genre, or portable translation. GDT559 is a primary predecessor whose 157/157 result motivates the question; the proposal retains that result as unconfirmed historical evidence.
